title: Pregnancy Recipes: Iron-and-Folate Bowls You Can Cook in 30 Minutes
excerpt: Three tasty recipes pairing heme/non-heme iron with vitamin C — Vietnamese-inspired bowls with clear portions and food-safety notes.
content:
## Introduction
When pregnant, it's essential to provide enough iron and folate to ensure the health of both mother and baby. Iron helps create red blood cells, while folate supports fetal development. In this article, we'll introduce three recipes rich in iron and folate that can be cooked in 30 minutes, suitable for pregnant women.

## Recipe 1: Grilled Chicken and Vegetable Bowl
* 100g grilled chicken (iron: 1.5mg)
* 1 cup cooked white rice
* 1 cup mixed vegetables (carrots, green beans, broccoli)
* 1 orange (vitamin C: 70mg)
* Note: Choose cooked chicken and washed vegetables to ensure food safety.

## Recipe 2: Beef and Water Spinach Stir-Fry Bowl
* 100g beef stir-fry (iron: 2.5mg)
* 1 cup cooked white rice
* 1 cup water spinach (vitamin C: 50mg)
* 1 lemon (vitamin C: 30mg)
* Note: Choose cooked beef and washed water spinach to ensure food safety.

## Recipe 3: Vegetarian Red Bean and Kale Bowl
* 100g cooked red beans (iron: 2mg)
* 1 cup cooked white rice
* 1 cup kale (vitamin C: 40mg)
* 1 orange (vitamin C: 70mg)
* Note: Choose cooked red beans and washed kale to ensure food safety.

## Combining Iron with Vitamin C
To enhance iron absorption, combine iron with vitamin C. Vitamin C helps convert iron into a absorbable form. Foods rich in vitamin C include oranges, lemons, vegetables, and fruits.

## Food Safety Notes
When pregnant, it's crucial to follow food safety guidelines to avoid bacterial infections and other health issues. Choose cooked food, wash vegetables thoroughly, and store food properly.

## Conclusion
The three recipes above provide sufficient iron and folate for pregnant women and can be cooked in 30 minutes. Combine iron with vitamin C to enhance absorption. Additionally, follow food safety guidelines to ensure the health of both mother and baby. For more information on [pregnancy meal planning](/blog/pregnancy-meal-planner), visit our website.

## When to Seek Help
If you have any questions or concerns about your health or your baby's health, consult your doctor or a registered dietitian for personalized advice.
